newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Nov COB electricity ends up amid softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Nov COB electricity ends up amid softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX California-Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures for November delivery settled higher Tuesday despite softer cash market prices in the western U.S., market sources said.

"The biggest thing was that futures came off with lower BPA (Bonneville Power Administration) prices," said a New York futures broker, adding some local traders who had long positions were rattled by the BPA cut.
BPA's firm, on peak prices for Wednesday delivery in the Northwest (ex-transmission) were at $17.62 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Monday's $21.00 for Tuesday delivery.
November COB futures settled up seven cents at $17.51 a MWh after hitting a session high of $17.90. December COB also finished up seven cents at $18.62. Most deferred COB ended flat to lower.
November PV futures finished unchanged from Monday's settlement of $16.60 a MWh. Other PV months also finished flat from Monday.
Despite ending off from the day's high, November COB could test the $18.00 level Wednesday, market sources said.
The latest forecasts showed the western U.S. would receive warmer to much warmer-than-normal autumn weather next week.
NYMEX estimated 360 COB and 12 PV contracts were sold Tuesday.
